prediction.raw: 0 I think it's wrong to keep old love letters as a backup plan in case you get tired of your husband. This approach can be seen as a form of emotional insurance, where you're holding onto past relationships as a potential escape route from your current one. This mindset can undermine the commitment and trust that are essential to a healthy marriage. Keeping old love letters can also serve as a reminder of past feelings and connections, which can be distracting and potentially damaging to your current relationship. It's essential to focus on nurturing and strengthening your marriage, rather than holding onto memories of past loves. Additionally, this approach can be perceived as a lack of commitment to your current partner and the relationship you've built together. A healthy marriage requires effort, communication, and dedication from both partners. Instead of keeping old love letters as a safety net, it's more productive to address any issues or concerns you may have with your husband and work together to strengthen your relationship.
